chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat ibn Ayyub, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abdul Malik ibn A'yan, who said:

I rose from the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), supported myself on my hand, and wept. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the matter with you?' I said: 'I used to hope that I would attain this Command (Al-Amr) while I had strength.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you not pleased that your enemies kill one another while you are safe in your houses? Indeed, if that were to happen, a man from among you would be given the strength of forty men, and your hearts would become like blocks of iron; if thrown against mountains, they would uproot them. And you would be the pillars of the earth and its treasurers.'

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The Command (referring to the rise of the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the strength of people during the time of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) contrasts the current era of relative safety with the future era of the Qaim, where believers will possess the strength of forty men and hearts of iron to establish divine justice. This narration highlights the transformative power of the Mahdi's rule, where ordinary individuals become the 'pillars and custodians of the earth,' fulfilling the prophetic promise of global equity. The Imam’s comfort underscores that the delay in the Qaim's appearance is not a denial of their potential, but a period of preparation for a time when they will actively uphold the earth's order.
